criteria.rationale: Verified mutable owner-controlled temp roots, permission recovery, delivered INT and TERM, absolute paths with relative TMPDIR and CDPATH, and real Docker composition. SIGKILL cannot be trapped. R3 deliberately checks plain lines or reviewed whole-file pins and does not prove arbitrary shell. Declared identity and unsigned attestations are not authenticated session provenance.

No Go concurrency contract changed. Each process owns a distinct mktemp root. Independent lifecycle probes exit 130 and 143 on delivered INT and TERM and leave caller TMPDIR empty; the missing-handler counterfactual fails the gate.

No API, MCP, schema or event contract changed. The sourced shell dependency is delivered to the measurement container in quickstart/lib sibling directories. The real container executes the installed release and the documented quickstart successfully.

Success, assertion failure, set-e error, unset variable and restricted 0400/0000 descendants clean up. Missing or late/commented/indented/conditional helper init, changed pins and stale pins produce failing gates. Docker removal failure no longer skips filesystem cleanup.

Source and init precede allocations in all three scripts; CLI options and assertions are preserved. CI, local verifier, the registered integration producer and the measurement consumer agree. Real Docker measurement passes with pose 7.4.1; the original cleanup trap fails the independent Docker-error control.

The gate identifies missing helper adoption, changed pins and obsolete pins with actionable paths. Setup markers and exact signal exit codes prevent vacuous cleanup success. Compact evidence retains command exits, scoped facts and external full-output SHA-256 without credentials.

Three scripts pass from their supported working directories and with binary/previous options, using absolute and relative caller TMPDIR. Exporting an absolute owned TMPDIR preserves ordinary Go/curl/git behavior. The copied quickstart and helper now execute in the existing container producer.

Global strict validation passes 137/137, baseline vet and complete Go tests pass, and independent permission/failure/signal, original-script, pin-mutation and real-script probes agree. F8 and F9 are resolved by actual Docker execution and old/new failure controls; no new finding remains.

Executed provider/consumer assessment and direct shell consumers. Its 63 pre-existing unobserved MCP-consumer observations are unchanged; this delivery changes no MCP contract. Matrix, CI, local verification, copied helper layout and real Docker execution exercise the changed boundaries.

D1 addresses the omitted-cleanup cause by exporting one owned TMPDIR and removing that root on exit, including child work. The observed validation-check delta exercises this choice and the authorized R3 omission/pin guard. Staging the helper fixes the actual copied-script dependency rather than weakening assertions.

The spec accurately describes the authorized R3 reduction and reviewed pin workflow. Helper composition documentation names pose_test_tmp_remove. Final closeout records actual producers, independent review and limits; prior rejected rounds remain in Git history.

Restricted entries are made owner-accessible before removal; error and signal exits still clean up. CDPATH is neutralized during absolute-root resolution. A failed Docker removal preserves the original failing status and still removes host temporary files. Pins give the reviewer an explicit re-review and repin path.

R1 is supported by the integration producer and independent mutable-state failure/permission/signal/CDPATH probes. R2 is supported by all three real script executions and option/cwd variants with empty TMPDIR. Revised R3 is supported by original-script failures, seven invalid helper forms, ten changed pins, obsolete pins and explicit repin controls.

Maintainer-authorized review covers this hygiene spec outside B01-B44 and the explicit R3 rescope, without production Go, policy, capability or adoption edits. agent:independent- is the engine-required declaration until pose-delegated-review-run-provenance replaces it. This Codex/OpenAI execution is another vendor than the Claude/Anthropic implementer. Identity is declared; pose-dist attestations are unsigned.

Owned mktemp roots and quoted paths contain child temporary data. Permission recovery precedes recursive removal; absolute paths avoid cwd and CDPATH confusion. No secret was printed. Hash pins detect file changes and do not authenticate reviewer identity or prove arbitrary-shell cleanup.

D1 is smaller and more reliable than maintaining every temporary allocation in three separate traps, while covering child work. The maintainer reduced an unbounded textual-shell analysis to a small adoption/pin guard. No new dependency or speculative engine framework is introduced; a real-script leak or assertion regression would falsify approval.
